instrument_name: RSMo 290.230 Prevailing wage rates required on public works
figure_or_rule_carried: State prevailing wage law exists (RSMo 290.210-290.340): prevailing hourly rate for public works; 2x on Sunday/holiday; 1.5x overtime (>10h/day or >40h/week); not applicable if project cost <= 75,000

instrument_name: RSMo 290.080 Semimonthly pay; statement of deductions
figure_or_rule_carried: Corporations pay at least semimonthly within 16 days of period close; furnish employee at least once a month a statement showing total amount of deductions (with check or separately); violation = misdemeanor, fine 50-500 per offense
Employer keeps 3 years: name, address, occupation, rate of pay, amount paid each pay period, hours worked per day and week; no itemized pay-statement duty in this section
Index lists 290.080 (statement of deductions), 290.210-290.340 (prevailing wage), 290.500-290.530 (minimum wage); no other pay-statement section and no paid-leave/disability programme in the chapter

instrument_name: Missouri DES Tax Rates page (new employer rates, taxable wage base)
authority: Missouri DOLIR, Division of Employment Security
article_or_section: Beginning Tax Rates; Taxable Wage Base; Automation Adjustment
figure_or_rule_carried: 2026 taxable wage limitation 9,000 (2025 9,500); new employer rate 2026 = 2.376% (all others, mining, construction), 1.00% 501(c)(3); experience range 0.0%-6.0%; automation adjustment up to 0.020% redirected from Q1 taxes (no extra amount due); employer-paid, no employee contribution described; RSMo 288.036(2) base range 7,000-13,000

instrument_name: City of St. Louis Employer Withholding and Payroll Expense Tax Information
authority: City of St. Louis Collector of Revenue
figure_or_rule_carried: Earnings tax withholding 1% on wages of employees living or working in St. Louis City (resident employers withhold on all employees); Payroll Expense Tax 0.5% paid by employer; both filed quarterly on W-10/P-10 (due Jan 31, Apr 30, Jul 31, Oct 31); administered by the Collector of Revenue, separate from the state return

instrument_name: Kansas City MO Tax FAQs + Tax Guide for Nonresident Businesses (earnings tax)
authority: City of Kansas City, Missouri Finance Department
figure_or_rule_carried: KC city FAQ refers to the one percent earnings tax; nonresident employers may voluntarily withhold (Form RD-100 registration) and then must withhold for resident employees and nonresident employees working in KC; city code Ch. 68 Art. VI; city-administered, not on state return. Rate wording only from FAQ question text; the mandatory-withholding page was not read

instrument_name: Missouri DES Power of Attorney page (UI tax/claims representative)
authority: Missouri DOLIR, Division of Employment Security
figure_or_rule_carried: Taxpayer may appoint a representative for UI tax and/or claims matters (except DES appeals) by signed written agreement; DES provides a POA form that may be used; send to Liability Unit (P.O. Box 59, Jefferson City MO 65104-0059; fax 573-751-3900; EmployerAddressChange@labor.mo.gov). Form number MODES-4444 appears only in a search listing, not in the page text read

3.5% flat rate; 2026 standard deduction 3,360; method: wages x annual periods - std deduction, x 3.5%, / periods; employee with more than one W-2 may need extra 117.60; sheet states NO rounding rule (examples show 104.65 in cents and 47 in whole dollars)

instrument_name: Kentucky Department of Revenue Business page (business tax list; local occupational taxes statement)
figure_or_rule_carried: Revenue Department states it does not administer local occupational, net profits or gross receipts taxes (directs to Kentucky Occupational License Association); the state business-tax list (employer payroll withholding, nonresident withholding, etc.) shows no SDI/PFML-type levy administered by Revenue

instrument_name: Denver Tax Guide Topic 61 Occupational Privilege Taxes (OPT)
authority: City and County of Denver Department of Finance
figure_or_rule_carried: Denver OPT: employee tax 5.75 per month withheld by employer when employee earns at least 500 in the month; employer business OPT 4.00 per month per taxable employee; Denver Treasury, not the state return; Aurora head tax referred to as a separate jurisdiction. Snapshot 2025-07-31 (2026 edition not located)

instrument_name: Colorado OSA Public Projects Defined / Prevailing Wage on Public Projects
authority: Colorado Office of the State Architect (DPA)
figure_or_rule_carried: State prevailing wage exists: contractors on public projects of 500,000 or more pay employees weekly and comply with 24-92-209 enforcement; part 2 does not apply to federally funded contracts; complaints go through contracting agency to CDLE. CDLE prevailing-wages page returned Access denied (gated)

instrument_name: CDLE How to Manage Third Party Administrator (TPA) Relationships (MyUI Employer+)
authority: Colorado Department of Labor and Employment
figure_or_rule_carried: UI third-party authorization is online: employer assigns TPA by TPA ID in MyUI Employer+ (Account Maintenance > TPA authorization); start dates at quarter start, end dates at quarter end; roles per reporting unit; no paper form on this page

instrument_name: Alabama Department of Labor - Wage and Hour Info
figure_or_rule_carried: Official statement: Alabama does not have any state laws governing wage and hour issues; employers follow the federal Wage and Hour Division (topics include wages, recordkeeping, deductions, government contracts); only child labor has state law. Supports no state pay-statement statute and no state prevailing-wage law
